Historians use this name for the wave of anticlerical violence — killings and church arson — carried out by leftist groups during the Spanish Civil War; what's it called?
Golden age of arcade video games
Red Terror (Spain): Assassinations during the Spanish Civil War.
As Colombia's Minister of Justice, he cracked down on cocaine traffickers until he was assassinated on the orders of a notorious drug baron in 1984 — who was he?
Rodrigo Lara Bonilla: Colombian lawyer and politician (1946-1984)
The oldest daughter of her husband's own uncle, this woman was the wife of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein and mother to sons Uday and Qusay — who is she?
Sajida Talfah: First wife of Saddam Hussein.

Proclaimed in 1852 when a president crowned himself Napoleon III, this 18-year regime built out a national railway network even as historians later judged its foreign policy a failure — what was this government called?
Second French Empire: France under Napoleon III (1852–1870)
Currently Japan's Minister of Defense, this LDP lawmaker representing Kanagawa is the son of a former prime minister and once worked as his father's political secretary — who is he?
Married to the youngest sibling of King Charles III since 1999, this member of the British royal family previously worked in public relations before her wedding at Windsor Castle — who is she?
Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh: Member of the British royal family (born 1965)

This Prince of Kiev, who ruled from 945 to 972, conquered rival Slavic tribes and helped bring down both Khazaria and the First Bulgarian Empire, carving out the largest state in Europe at the time — who was he?
Sviatoslav I: Prince of Kiev from 945 to 972. Following the death of his father Igor in 945, Sviatoslav's mother Olga reigned as regent in Kiev until 962.
An economist educated at Cambridge, he served as Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister and central bank chairman before becoming the country's ninth president in 2023 — who is he?

Tharman Shanmugaratnam: President of Singapore since 2023. Tharman Shanmugaratnam (born 25 February 1957) is a Singaporean politician and economist who has served as the ninth president of Singapore since 2023.

Nicknamed 'The Tiger of Malaya' after conquering the peninsula and a nearby island stronghold in just 70 days, this WWII Japanese general later held out on Luzon until his country's surrender in 1945 — who is he?
Tomoyuki Yamashita: Japanese officer and war criminal (1885–1946)
A combat veteran of the Second Chechen War who once commanded the 58th Combined Arms Army, he has run the General Staff of Russia's Armed Forces since 2012. Which Russian general is this?
Controlled until 2023 by Yevgeny Prigozhin, this Russian state-funded private military company first emerged fighting in the Donbas war — which group?
Wagner Group: Russian private military company. The Wagner Group has used infrastructure of the Russian Armed Forces.
Dying just 31 days into office in 1841, this ninth U.S. president holds the record for shortest term ever served — who is he?
William Henry Harrison: President of the United States in 1841.
Cairo-born and a founding member of Fatah, he chaired the PLO from 1969 until his death in 2004 — which Palestinian leader?
Yasser Arafat: President of Palestine from 1989 to 2004.
Elected mayor of Guatemala City six times, this president's crowning achievement was the 1996 peace accord that ended his country's 36-year civil war — who was he?
Which of these people was born first?
Zhuge Liang (born 181) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four began earliest?
Python (programming language) (founded 1991) is the earliest of the four. Python supports multiple programming paradigms but with an emphasis on object-oriented programming and dynamic typing.
Which one below was established earliest?
MATLAB (founded 1984) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Norman Ramsey Jr. is a physicist.
Who among these is a chemist?
Ivan Pavlov is a chemist. Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
What is the atomic number of Oganesson?
Oganesson: Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
In what year was Michael Rockefeller born?
Michael Rockefeller: Michael Clark Rockefeller (May 18, 1938; disappeared November 19, 1961) was an American anthropologist and art collector and member of the Rockefeller family.
In what year was William James Sidis born?
William James Sidis: Born to Boris Sidis, a prominent psychiatrist, and Sarah Mandelbaum Sidis, a physician, Sidis demonstrated extraordinary intellectual capabilities from infancy.
In what year was Wernher von Braun born?
Wernher von Braun: As a young man, von Braun worked in Nazi Germany's rocket development program.
In what year did Carl Linnaeus die?
Carl Linnaeus: Linnaeus was the son of a curate and was born in Råshult, in the countryside of Småland, southern Sweden.
In what year did Antoine Lavoisier die?
Antoine Lavoisier: It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
In what year was Palladium discovered?
Palladium: Palladium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Pd and atomic number 46.
In what year was Chromium discovered?
Chromium: Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
Mil Mi-28: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.
In which country did the Hawker Hurricane take place?
Hawker Hurricane: United Kingdom. The Air Ministry ordered Hawker's Interceptor Monoplane in late 1934, and the prototype Hurricane K5083 performed its maiden flight on 6 November 1935.
Who is credited with discovering Telescopium?
Telescopium: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is a Latinized form of the Greek word for telescope.
Who is credited with discovering Spontaneous generation?
Spontaneous generation: Anaximander. It was hypothesized that certain forms, such as fleas, could arise from inanimate matter such as dust, or that maggots could arise from dead flesh.
Who is credited with discovering SN 1987A?
SN 1987A: Ian Shelton. SN 1987A was a Type II supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
This Onmyōdō master advised Heian emperors on astrology and spiritual matters; a Kyoto shrine and an Osaka train station now honor him — who is he?
Abe no Seimei (February 21, 921 AD - October 31, 1005) was a Japanese onmyji, a court official and specialist of Onmyd, during the middle of the Heian period.
Which diverse group of aquatic photosynthetic organisms excludes land plants but includes seaweeds that can grow up to 50 metres long?
Algae (UK also; sing.: alga) are any of a large and diverse group of photosynthetic organisms.
This type of long-term arthritis causes inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis, with lower back pain as its hallmark symptom. What condition is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.

Around 1920, when the energy source of stars was a complete mystery, which English astrophysicist boldly and correctly guessed it was the fusion of hydrogen into helium — and lent his name to a natural ceiling on a star's brightness?
Arthur Eddington (28 December 1882 - 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
The third-most-produced bomber in history, this American four-engine heavy bomber dominated the European Theater and dropped more bombs than any other plane in WWII — which aircraft is it?
Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC).

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Portuguese explorers carried this tropical American tree to India in the 16th century; today Ivory Coast and India lead a 3.9-million-ton global harvest of its nut — what is it?
Cashew is the common name of a tropical evergreen tree Anacardium occidentale, in the family Anacardiaceae.
Born in 1847, this American wore three hats at once — psychologist, logician, and mathematician. Who was she?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 - March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
This activity involves designing algorithms and writing code in high-level languages so a machine can follow step-by-step instructions to perform tasks. What is it?
Computer programming is the composition of sequences of instructions, called programs, that computers can follow to perform tasks.

This closed sac within the body has a distinct wall of cells that are structurally abnormal compared to surrounding tissue, and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — unlike a pus-filled abscess, what is it called?
Cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.
Bred around 1890 in Thuringia by a tax collector seeking a loyal protector, this German working-dog breed is known in North America by a slightly different two-word name — which breed?
Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type.
Working with George de Hevesy, this Hungarian chemist theorized that diffusion speed depends on a nuclide's mass and became the world's go-to expert at preparing polonium — who was she?
Elizabeth Rona (20 March 1890 - 27 July 1981) was a Hungarian nuclear chemist, known for her work with radioactive isotopes.

Built by a consortium of Airbus, BAE Systems and Leonardo for four NATO nations, this twin-engine canard delta-wing fighter grew out of the 1983 Future European Fighter Aircraft programme — which jet?
Eurofighter Typhoon is a European multinational twin-engine, supersonic, canard delta wing, multirole fighter.
Part of the dog family yet famous for a pointed snout and a brush-like tail, the 'true' members of this group belong to the genus Vulpes — what creature is it?
Fox are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae.
Caught from a tiny waterborne protist and common in travelers and children, it brings fatty, sticky diarrhea and abdominal pain a week or three after exposure — what is this parasitic illness?
Giardiasis is a parasitic disease caused by the protist enteropathogen Giardia duodenalis (also known as G. lamblia).
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is a fisheries staple in northern Europe, often smoked into varieties like Finnan haddie and the Arbroath smokie — what is it?
Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.
First unearthed in 1994 in Spain's Gran Dolina cave, this Early Pleistocene human was named 'pioneer man' because it was among the first to settle Western Europe. Which species is it?

Homo antecessor (Latin for 'pioneer man') is an extinct species of archaic human recorded in the Spanish Sierra de Atapuerca, a productive archaeological site, from 1.2 to 0.8 million years ago during the Early Pleistocene.
More than 20 types make up this genetic skin condition, whose Greek-derived name means "fish" — a nod to its hallmark dry, thickened, scaly texture — which disorder?
Ichthyosis is a family of genetic skin disorders characterized by dry, thickened, scaly skin.
This billionaire computer programmer co-founded WhatsApp before selling it to Facebook for $19.3 billion in 2014 — who is he?
Jan Koum (born February 24, 1976) is an American billionaire businessman and computer programmer.
Linked to a herpesvirus and immune suppression, this cancer causing purple skin lesions was already being described by Hippocrates in the 300s BC — which condition?
Kaposi's sarcoma (KS) is a type of cancer that can form masses on the skin, in lymph nodes, in the mouth, or in other organs.
Caused by a specific type of waterborne bacteria, this form of atypical pneumonia brings cough, fever, muscle pain, and headache within days of exposure — what's it called?
Legionnaires' disease is a form of atypical pneumonia caused by any species of Legionella bacteria, quite often Legionella pneumophila.

Fatigue, memory problems, breathlessness, and sleep trouble that the WHO marks as setting in three months after infection — symptoms that vanish and reappear for weeks or years. What condition is this?
Long COVID is a group of health problems persisting or developing after an initial period of COVID19 from 2 infection.
This Silicon Valley venture capitalist co-created the pioneering Mosaic browser, co-founded Netscape, and later became an advisor to Donald Trump in 2024 — who is he?
Marc Andreessen (an-; born July 9, 1971) is an American businessman, venture capitalist, and former software engineer.
Sold dissolved in solution or shipped anhydrous in pressurized railcars, this simplest primary amine reeks like rotten fish — what compound is it?
Methylamine is an organic compound with a formula of CH5N or CH3NH2.
First documented with ice cream and water by a Tanzanian student and his professor in the 1960s, this contested observation says warmer liquids can outrace colder ones to freezing — what's it called?
Mpemba effect is the observation that very hot liquids or colloids (such as ice cream) can freeze more quickly than colder ones, for similar volumes and surrounding conditions.
Found in tobacco and trace amounts of tomatoes and eggplants, this nightshade alkaloid is used recreationally as a stimulant yet acts as a deadly neurotoxin to insects — what is it?
Nicotine is an alkaloid found primarily in plants of the nightshade family, notably in tobacco; it is also synthesized.
These red-haired great apes once roamed all of Southeast Asia but now cling to just Borneo and Sumatra — and in 2017 scientists confirmed a brand-new third species among them. Which animal is it?
Orangutan are great apes native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia.
This British theoretical physicist, one of the founders of quantum mechanics, coined the term 'quantum electrodynamics' and shared the 1933 Nobel Prize in Physics with Erwin Schrödinger — who is he?
Paul Dirac (dih-RAK; 8 August 1902 - 20 October 1984) was a British theoretical physicist who is considered to be one of the founders of quantum mechanics.
This branch of linguistics is concerned with how speech sounds are physically produced, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived by listeners — name the field?
Phonetics is a branch of linguistics that mainly concerns the articulation, sound wave properties, and perception of speech sounds.
Native to Southeast Asia and a natural, non-hybrid ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange, this largest of all citrus fruits also goes by the name 'shaddock' — what is it?
Pomelo (PUM-; or pummelo, Citrus maxima), also known as a shaddock, is the largest citrus fruit.
Which industry has expanded from traditional books and newspapers to e-books, websites, and video games, with giants like Thomson Reuters and News Corp among its biggest players?
Publishing is the process of making information, literature, music, software, and other content, whether in physical or digital form, available to the public for sale or free of charge.
This long-term autoimmune disorder leaves joints warm, swollen and painful — typically the same ones on both sides of the body — and can stiffen worse after rest. What is it?
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a long-term autoimmune disorder that primarily affects joints.
Which genus of 20 to 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae produces both a fragrant white flower cluster and a dark berry, each with their own distinct common name?

Sambucus is a genus of between 20 and 30 species of flowering plants in the family Adoxaceae. The various species are commonly referred to as elder, with the flowers as elderflower, and the fruit as elderberry.
Cartilaginous and toothy, these fish are the sister group to the rays and skates and trace their ancestors to the Devonian Period — what are they?

Shark are a group of elasmobranch cartilaginous fishes characterized by a ribless endoskeleton, dermal denticles, five to seven gill slits on each side, and pectoral fins that are not fused to the head.
These eight-legged arachnids inject venom through their fangs and extrude silk from spinnerets, ranking as the largest order in their class — what are they?
Spider (order Araneae) are air-breathing arthropods that have eight limbs, chelicerae with fangs generally able to inject venom, and spinnerets that extrude silk.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Known also as sight or eyesight, this sense lets the body detect photons and build a picture of its environment using daytime or night modes — what is it?
Visual perception is the ability to detect light and use it to form an image of the surrounding environment.
Known for a rapid side-to-side flight just before landing and living only in colonies, these black-and-yellow social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula go by what North American name?
Yellowjacket is the common name in North America for predatory social wasps of the genera Vespula and Dolichovespula.
A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Formed when hydrogen atoms in ammonia are swapped out for carbon-based groups, which class of nitrogen-containing organic compounds includes aniline as its simplest aromatic member?
Amine: Chemical compounds and groups containing nitrogen with a lone pair (:N)
Native to Africa, India, the Middle East and Central Asia, these fleet-footed members of the family Bovidae aren't actually one single evolutionary group — what are they?
Related to anteaters and sloths, this armored mammal ranges from a giant species over a meter long to a tiny pink 'fairy' species barely 13 centimeters — what animal is it?
Armadillo: Placental mammals in the order Cingulata.
Native to the Americas and prized for thousands of years for its unusually oily fruit, this evergreen of the laurel family bears what's botanically a giant berry around a single seed — what is it?
Avocado: Species of flowering plant in the laurel family.
Sometimes called the common, lawn, or English variety, this European plant is considered the archetypal member of the daisy family — what's its scientific name?

Bellis perennis: Species of plant in the daisy family. Bellis perennis ( BEL-iss pə-REN-iss), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Typically housed in the head near the organs for vision, hearing, and smell, this organ processes thought and cognition while coordinating muscle activity — which organ?
Brain: Organ central to the nervous system.
Native to the Americas from Patagonia to western Canada, members of this succulent plant family thrive in the bone-dry Atacama Desert — what are they?
Cactus: Family of mostly succulent plants, adapted to dry environments.

A German child prodigy turned director of the Göttingen Observatory, this mathematician, astronomer, and physicist made landmark contributions across number theory, algebra, statistics, and probability — who is he?
Carl Friedrich Gauss: German polymath and scholar (1777–1855)
This Italian physician who died in 1909 is considered the founder of modern criminology, arguing that 'born criminals' could be spotted by physical defects — who is he?
Add this steely-grey transition metal (atomic number 24) to steel and you get stainless; polish it and it reflects nearly 70% of visible light without tarnishing. Which element is it?
Chromium: Chemical element with atomic number 24 (Cr)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Its Greek name literally means 'boat beard,' describing how its hairy spikelets project from boat-shaped sheaths — better known by a common name evoking a citrus scent, what is this grass genus?
First patented in Germany in 1920 and later synthesized by an American chemist in 1932, this semi-synthetic opioid is roughly ten times more potent than morphine — what is it called?
Desomorphine: Semi-synthetic opioid, morphine analogue. It was first discovered and patented in Germany by a German team working for Knoll in 1920 but was not generally recognized.
Despite its common names, this evergreen conifer isn't a true member of the pine, spruce, or hemlock genera, yet stands as the tallest species in its own family — what is it?
Douglas fir: Species of tree. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine.
This membrane-bound series of protein complexes shuttles electrons through redox reactions, building a proton gradient that ultimately powers the synthesis of ATP — what's it called?
Electron transport chain: Energy-producing metabolic pathway.
Named from the Greek for 'red skin,' this bacterial infection produces a raised, sharply defined, bright-red rash typically on the face or legs — what's the condition?
Erysipelas: Human disease from a bacterial infection of the skin.
Also nicknamed the 'baum' or 'sweet' variety, this mustelid species ranges across much of the continent into Asia Minor, the Caucasus, and parts of Iran, Iraq, and Syria. What animal is it?
European pine marten: Species of mammal in the mustelid family.
This antiandrogen medication lowers DHT production by about 70 percent and is used to treat pattern hair loss and an enlarged prostate — which drug?

Finasteride: Antiandrogen medication. Finasteride, sold under the brand names Proscar and Propecia among others, is a medication used to treat pattern hair loss and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH).

Sent by his father to work in a Manchester cotton mill, this German theorist co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Karl Marx and later finished editing Das Kapital after his friend's death — who was he?
Friedrich Engels: German philosopher and socialist (1820–1895)

Arriving late to a lecture, this mathematician copied down two famous unsolved problems in statistics, mistook them for homework — and solved them; he's better known for inventing the simplex algorithm for linear programming. Who was he?
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and earned the nickname 'the last universal genius' — who is he?
This protein filament that grows from follicles in the skin is one of the defining traits of mammals, and its removal or styling carries different meanings across cultures — what is it?
Hair: Protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis, or skin.

Famous for the ideas of "bounded rationality" and "satisficing," this remarkable scholar won both a Turing Award and a Nobel in Economics — bridging computer science, economics, and psychology. Who was he?
Herbert A. Simon: American academic and Nobel Laureate (1916–2001)

Found only in the Americas from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, these roughly 375 species pull off rapid, maneuverable flight thanks to an exceptional metabolism — and their males flaunt the widest plumage diversity of any bird — what are they?
This Russian-American engineer built the first successful four-engine aircraft in 1913 and went on to pioneer the modern helicopter — who was he?
Nicknamed 'Dr. Death,' this pathologist assisted at least 130 patients in dying and was convicted of murder after broadcasting one such case on television — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian: American pathologist and euthanasia activist (1928–2011)
The youngest division chief in GM history shepherded the Pontiac GTO before founding the motor company behind a stainless-steel sports car immortalized in Back to the Future — who was he?
John DeLorean: American automobile engineer and executive (1925–2005)
Sold under names like Toradol and Acular, this NSAID's use is capped at five days due to serious side-effect risk, with relief starting within an hour — what drug is it?
A genus of 47 flowering plant species in the sage family, prized for its fragrant oil and used in traditional medicine, cosmetics, and as a culinary herb across Mediterranean climates — which genus?
Lavandula: Genus of plants. Lavandula (common name lavender) is a genus of 47 known species of perennial flowering plants in the sage family, Lamiaceae.
Soft, movable, and painless, this benign fatty-tissue growth most often shows up under the skin on the upper back, shoulders, or abdomen — what is it?
Lipoma: Benign tumor made of fat tissue.
Native to China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and blooming in late summer after heavy rainfall, this plant's alternate names include the hurricane lily and the corpse flower — what is it?
Lycoris radiata: Species of plant. It is originally from China, Japan, Korea and Nepal and spread from there to the United States and elsewhere.
This American cultural anthropologist's 1928 fieldwork, Coming of Age in Samoa, made her a household name for exploring adolescence and sexuality in Pacific societies — who is she?
Nicknamed a 'semi-lunar' cartilage for its half-moon shape, this crescent-shaped structure cushions joints like the knee, wrist, and jaw — what is it?
Meniscus (anatomy): Fibrocartilaginous part of a bone joint.

An advanced modification of its Korean War-era predecessor, this Soviet transonic fighter — NATO reporting name 'Fresco' — was license-built in China and Poland, and remains in North Korean service today — which jet?
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Soviet jet fighter aircraft family.

Beginning as a tightly compressed gray sponge before expanding into a pitted yellow-brown honeycomb atop a hollow white stem, which springtime fungus is a prized edible found near old orchards and hardwoods?
Morchella esculenta: Species of fungus. The pits are rounded and irregularly arranged.
Sold under the brand name Deca-Durabolin, this anabolic steroid is prescribed for conditions like anemia and osteoporosis despite masculinizing side effects — which compound?
Nandrolone: Androgenic Anabolic steroid. Nandrolone, also known as 19-nortestosterone, is an endogenous androgen.
Humphry Davy coined this colorless gas's cheerful nickname for the euphoria it brings, and it still earns a spot on the WHO's Essential Medicines list for dentistry and surgery. What is it?
Nitrous oxide: Colourless non-flammable greenhouse gas.

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
A famous singer known for her CCTV New Year's Gala appearances, she has served as China's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?
Peng Liyuan: First Lady of China since 2012. Peng also sang the theme songs of several popular TV series, such as The Water Margin (1998).
With a phosphate-charged head and two fatty-acid tails joined by glycerol, this molecule builds neuron membranes and can decline up to 20% by age 80 — what is it?
Sitting less than a degree from the north celestial pole, this yellow supergiant is famously steady for navigation — but is secretly a triple star system. What is it?
Polaris: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor.

Diagnosed in about 8% of male urology visits in the US, this umbrella term covers several bacterial and non-bacterial pelvic conditions, despite its name not always involving actual inflammation — which condition?
Prostatitis: Medical condition. Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.
Named partly for Jack Northrop, designer of a tailless aircraft, which genus of enormous azhdarchid pterosaur is a top candidate for the largest flying animal ever?
Quetzalcoatlus: Genus of azhdarchid pterosaurs from the Late Cretaceous.
Native to East Asia but a notorious invasive pest in Europe and North America, this knotweed has won over beekeepers and foragers alike, its young stems tasting of lemony rhubarb. What plant is it?
Native to Eurasia and commonly known simply as the raspberry, this red-fruited bramble is widely cultivated across temperate regions — what species is it?
Nicknamed 'snail fever,' this tropical disease is caused by a parasitic flatworm picked up from freshwater contaminated by infected snails — what is it?
Schistosomiasis: Human disease caused by parasitic worms called schistosomes.
The first woman on Facebook's board, she turned the company profitable as its long-serving COO and founded LeanIn.Org — who is she?
Once called 'hyposulphite of soda,' this reducing agent treats cyanide poisoning and served as photography's key fixer in the 19th century — what compound?
Sodium thiosulfate: Chemical compound. Sodium thiosulfate (sodium thiosulphate) is an inorganic compound with the formula Na2S2O3·xH2O.
For 30 years this English theoretical astrophysicist held Cambridge's most prestigious academic post—the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics. Who?
Derived from a Greek word meaning 'concurrence,' this medical term describes a set of signs and symptoms that tend to occur together — what is it called?
Syndrome: Association of several clinically recognizable features.
Also sold under the name dronabinol, this principal psychoactive compound in cannabis is prescribed to relieve chemotherapy-induced nausea and HIV/AIDS-related appetite loss — what is it?
Tetrahydrocannabinol: Psychoactive component of cannabis. It is the principal psychoactive constituent of Cannabis and one of at least 113 total cannabinoids identified on the plant.
Sitting between cells and organs in the body's organization, this assembly of similar cells and their extracellular matrix takes its English name from a French word meaning 'to weave' — what is it?
Tissue (biology): Group of similar cells performing a specific function.
Element 74 boasts the highest melting point of any known element — a scorching 3,422 °C — and carries the symbol W from its German name. Which metal is it?
Tungsten: Chemical element with atomic number 74 (W)
This abnormal enlargement of veins in the scrotum is the most common correctable cause of male infertility, affecting around 15% of all men — what is it called?
Varicocele: Abnormal enlargement of the pampiniform plexus veins in the scrotum.

This German American aerospace engineer and space architect (1912–1977) initially worked in Nazi Germany's rocket development program and later led rocket and space technology development in the US — who is he?
Wernher von Braun: German American aerospace engineer (1912–1977). The V-2 became the first artificial object to travel into space by crossing the Kármán line on 20 June 1944.
